# Results -- Study 224 (Monday Effect) on the real total-return tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe: measure the
**per-weekday mean daily return** (close-to-close) on **total-return** SPY, the
**Monday-vs-rest** contrast with HAC *t*-stats, a **pre-2000 vs post-2000** split *with a
test of the change*, and literal **"buy Monday only" / "skip Monday"** timers net of **1 bp**
per switch against buy-and-hold. Day-of-week is calendar-known, so there is **no execution
lag**. As-of **2026-06-16**; match the fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tape.*

## Data stamp

| Series | Window | Rows | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| SPY (total return) | 1993-01-29 -> 2026-06-12 | 8,400 | `eb1569cc9e97` |

## Per-weekday mean daily return (whole sample)

| Weekday | Mean (bps) | n | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **Mon** | **+5.64** | 1,578 | +2.06 |
| Tue | +7.17 | 1,725 | +2.64 |
| Wed | +6.20 | 1,723 | +2.21 |
| Thu | +1.46 | 1,690 | +0.52 |
| Fri | +3.32 | 1,683 | +1.33 |

> **Monday is *positive* on this tape** (+5.64 bps), not the worst day. The classic
> Monday Effect -- negative close-to-close Monday returns -- is absent from the SPY era.

## The Monday-vs-rest contrast (whole sample)

| Contrast | Difference (bps) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| Monday -- rest | +1.08 | +0.36 |
| Tuesday -- rest | +3.03 | +1.00 |

Neither clears |*t*| = 2. Monday is not even the weakest day -- Thursday (+1.46 bps)
holds that title -- and the Monday contrast is positive, the *wrong sign* for the
classic Monday Effect.

## Pre-2000 vs post-2000 -- with a HAC test of the *change*

| Effect | Pre-2000 (bps) | Post-2000 (bps) | Change (bps) | HAC *t* (change) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Monday -- rest | +4.78 | +0.09 | -4.69 | -0.77 |

The Monday contrast is *positive in both halves*. The change HAC t = -0.77 means
we cannot certify a 'decay' -- the effect was never negative on this tape in the
first place. The classic French (1980) effect predates the SPY era entirely.

## The literal timers -- net of 1 bp/switch

| Arm | CAGR | Vol | Sharpe | Max drawdown | Time in mkt | Switches |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Buy Monday only | **1.34%** | 8.8% | **0.196** | -41.7% | 19% | 3,154 |
| Skip Monday | 7.30% | 16.4% | 0.512 | -48.9% | 81% | 3,155 |
| Buy & hold | **10.82%** | 18.6% | **0.646** | -55.2% | 100% | 0 |

## The decisive numbers

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Is Monday negative (the Monday Effect)? | **No** -- Monday is **+5.64 bps**, Monday-rest **+1.08 bps** (HAC *t* +0.36) |
| Is Monday the worst day? | **No** -- Thursday is weakest (+1.46 bps) |
| Did the Monday effect decay post-2000? | Change **-4.69 bps**, HAC *t* **-0.77** -- not significant; it was never negative |
| Buy-Monday CAGR vs buy-and-hold | **-9.47 pts/yr** (1.34% vs 10.82%) |
| Skip-Monday CAGR vs buy-and-hold | **-3.52 pts/yr** (7.30% vs 10.82%) |
| Buy-Monday / Skip-Monday Sharpe vs buy-and-hold | **-0.450 / -0.133** (both worse) |

## How to read it

- **Signal -> None.** Monday is *positive* and the contrast is +1.08 bps (HAC *t* +0.36),
  the wrong sign and nowhere near significance. There is no Monday Effect on this tape.
- **Tradability -> Mirage.** Both literal rules badly trail buy-and-hold. "Buy Monday only"
  loses **9.5 pts/yr** because it sits in cash 81% of the time and forfeits the equity
  premium; "skip Monday" loses **3.5 pts/yr** -- you can't beat the market by avoiding the
  day that turns out to be positive.
- **The claim -> Busted.** The classic Monday Effect (negative Monday) is not present on the
  1993-2026 SPY close-to-close tape, pre- *or* post-2000. French's (1980) finding is a
  pre-publication sample artefact.

python examples/verify.py   # real tape (this doc)
